speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand the nature of your condition, could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they worsen with activity?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic. Could you tell me if you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CK, AChR, MuSK, and Anti-Hu antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: NORMAL READINGS, CK: NORMAL READINGS, AChR: Present (elevated), MuSK: NORMAL READINGS, Anti-Hu: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, combined with the characteristic vertical diplopia, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
